standfirst: What this module calls, what it was built from, and where it stops. Every number on this page comes from a measurement file in the build directory; nothing is estimated.
lede01: One genus, and the first module in this family in which two features are called by splicing rather than by a profile.
p01: Amdoparvovirus is the only genus in the module; Aleutian mink disease virus is its type species. Five features are declared: NS1, NS2, NS3, and the capsid pair VP1 and VP2.

NS1 and VP1 carry copy_num. NS2 and NS3 do not, and cannot — they are declared special: splice and called from curated nucleotide references by get_splice_variant_features.pl, and a spliced feature is never treated as essential.

The literature is settled on this. AMDV transcribes from a single promoter and makes its small nonstructural proteins by alternative processing of the pre-mRNA (PMID 16378968); the abundant R2 message is tricistronic, carrying NS2 alongside VP1 and VP2 (PMID 17428872); and both NS2 and NS3 were confirmed to be expressed during infection, with NS3 at much lower levels (PMID 24606679).
lede02: Profiles are built from the annotation strings BV-BRC already carries; the splice references are built from the genomes themselves.
p02: Forty-four distinct annotation strings collapse onto the five feature names, over 841 source sequences. VP2 draws on eleven of them, NS2 on ten, NS1 and NS3 on eight each.

NS2's ten are the warning sign that started this build's hardest thread. They include nonstructural protein 3, NS3 and non-structural protein 3 alongside the NS2 spellings. The same protein is deposited under both names by different submitters, and the reverse is also true in the NS3 collection.

The three PSSM features — NS1, VP1 and VP2 — keep nine profiles between them. NS2 and NS3 have none: they are called from 227 and 43 nucleotide references, each a genomic slice with its splice donor and acceptor marked.
lede03: Each profile carries a bit-score floor and a length window; each splice feature carries a length window and nothing else.
p03: The PSSM floors are NS1 709, VP1 1,028 and VP2 1,056 bits. NS2 and NS3 carry no bit cutoff, no coverage cutoff and no extension flags, because none of those describes how a splice feature is called — a bit cutoff on a feature with no profile reads as a threshold someone chose and invites the next curator to tune it.

The splice references were not guessed. NS2's 227 references come from a two-exon build whose spliced product is 114 residues in 209 of them, and 47 reproduce their own genome's deposited NS2 exactly. NS3's 43 come from a second acceptor off the same donor, and 18 reproduce their own genome's deposited NS3 exactly.
lede04: Routing is a BLASTn of the query against the reference contigs.
p04: The module ships one reference contig, the fewest of any module in this family. That is enough here because the genus is narrow and its members are closely related to each other, but it is the module's thinnest margin: a divergent amdoparvovirus with no close relative to that single contig will not route at all.
lede05: Two measurements, two denominators: the tiles are the 41 exemplars drawn to span the genus, the paragraphs below are all 289 genomes that routed.
p05: Across the 289 genomes that routed: VP1 99.3%, VP2 99.3%, NS1 94.1%, NS2 84.4%, NS3 15.9%. VP1 and NS1 clear the 0.85 bar and carry copy_num; VP2 clears it on the raw rate but never stands alone — every one of its 287 calls sits inside a VP1 call, which is what a nested alternative start looks like — so it is blocked from being marked essential.

NS3's 15.9% is the honest figure. It is expressed at much lower levels than NS2, it is deposited by only a minority of submitters, and a reference is written only when the spliced translation can be placed against sequence. Where NS3 is called, the junction was found; where it is not, nothing was invented.
lede06: The panel is 300 genomes drawn from the module's own sample; it is not held out.
p06: 262 of 300 genomes carry no genome-level and no contig-level flag. Of the rest, 11 have no contig at all — the deposit is a protein record with no sequence to annotate — and 41 flags are a missing essential feature, 8 a contig with more than 1% ambiguous bases. There are two feature-level flags in the whole panel.
Set that against where this module was. With copy_num applied and NS2 and NS3 still called by profiles, 7 of 300 genomes were clean. The number is now 262.

The figure that matters most is not in the tiles: no two features are called at identical coordinates in any of the 300 genomes. Before this rebuild, NS1, NS2 and NS3 shared one set of coordinates in 274 of them. Read the headline percentage for what it is, though — the panel still contains the genome the single reference contig was taken from.
lede07: Three limits, each measured rather than supposed.
p07: A third spliced product exists and is not declared. The genus uses three acceptors off one donor. Two of them give NS2 at 114 residues and NS3 at 66 to 71; the third gives a product of 87 or 92 residues, deposited 28 times as NS2 and 4 times as NS3, all from AMDV itself. It has no agreed name, so declaring it under either would be choosing a side in a disagreement between submitters. It is recorded in UNASSIGNED_TRACKING.tsv instead.

NS3 is called in about a fifth of genomes. Its 43 references are what could be placed against sequence; a genome whose NS3 junction differs from all of them gets no NS3 call and no warning. Do not read an absent NS3 as evidence that the genome lacks the gene.
One reference contig. Routing has no redundancy here at all.
verdict07: Use this module for amdoparvovirus genomes. NS1, VP1 and VP2 are reliable. Treat an NS2 or NS3 call as a positive finding and their absence as no finding — and do not read the 87/92 residue product's absence as a gap, it is a naming dispute left open on purpose.
lede08: What the build turned up that was not expected.
p08: This module is the reason the family's NS features were re-examined at all. Applying copy_num dropped it to 7 of 300 genomes clean: NS2 was flagged "too many HSPs" in 288, and NS1, NS2 and NS3 sat on identical coordinates in 274. The call rate and the self-recall were perfect throughout, so nothing before that step looked wrong.

The cause was not the collections, which are clean — NS2 runs 80 to 116 residues across 145 deposits. It was that NS2 and NS3 share their first exon with NS1, so a short profile necessarily matches inside the NS1 open reading frame, and the start and stop extension then walked the call out to NS1's own boundaries. The printed NS2 translation was byte-for-byte NS1's: 600 residues against a declared maximum of 122.

Two things had to be true before that was visible. A feature's declared length window is never checked against a PSSM-called feature, and the test repository was running a caller eight weeks older than the kit's, in which the coverage cutoff was measured against the matched span rather than the profile — so it was always about 1.0 and never fired. Both are now recorded; the fix that shipped is the splice declaration, not a change to either.
lede09: What collapsing the vocabulary actually bought.
p09: 513 deposited protein strings across 120 genomes reduce to five feature names. The saturation curve on the companion page shows the deposited vocabulary still climbing with each genome added while the called vocabulary is flat at five.
One string resisted, two sequences: putative nonstructural protein. The 87/92 residue splice product is the larger unfinished item, and it is a naming question rather than a sequence one.
